parts.name: Cornice
parts.desc: A broad steel ledge that reaches further than any other assist, with no edge on it at all.
parts.rationale: Sibling of vane, the Tier 1 reach part. radAdd 0.0025 is exactly 25 percent of the 0 to 0.0020 span past the ceiling; smash 0.70 is 39 percent of the smash span below the floor, which is further, and it is the honest cost of a wide rolled lip that has no cutting face. Mass sits at the Tier 1 ceiling as part of the physical story of holding steel out at the rim, but the formal bill is smash because assist mass is nearly spin neutral in the sim. Beats vane only on radAdd and loses gearMul, absorb, smash and weight.

parts.name: Longspur
parts.desc: All the reach of a wide rim on a light frame, with nothing left over to cushion what comes back.
parts.rationale: Sibling of jag. Same 25 percent radAdd push as cornice but bought the other way, with absorb 0.68 at 35 percent of the absorb span below the floor, so every strike destabilises it about 35 percent harder through the 1/absorb term in tipA. Smash was trimmed to 1.10 and mass raised to 0.0042 so it is strictly worse than jag on gearMul, absorb, smash and weight and wins on reach alone.

parts.name: Teasel
parts.desc: A ring of fine hooked teeth that mesh with whatever they touch and pass every jolt straight to the tip.
parts.rationale: Sibling of hook, the Tier 1 spin thief. gearMul 2.15 is 24.6 percent of the 1.42 span past 1.80; absorb 0.66 is 39 percent of the absorb span below the floor, further than the push, and it is what a rim of bare teeth with no damping layer actually behaves like. Loses to hook on absorb, radAdd, smash and weight.

parts.name: Sprocket
parts.desc: A deep toothed collar that grinds spin off a rival but has no edge left to finish anyone.
parts.rationale: Sibling of hook, the same gearMul push as teasel with the opposite bill. Smash 0.70 is 39 percent of the span below the floor, and for a defense top that is a real loss because low smash shrinks jn, which is what shoves an attacker toward the lip and drives the 27 percent of finishes that are ringouts. Absorb 0.98 is deliberately below hook's 1.02 so it wins on gearMul only.

parts.name: Lacquer
parts.desc: A mirror rim that gives a rival nothing to grip and gives you nothing to hide behind.
parts.rationale: Sibling of slick. gearMul 0.28 is 26 percent below the 0.38 floor measured proportionally, because 25 percent of the gearMul span below the floor is a negative number and meaningless. Low grip protects a spin lead, since mu equalises spin from the faster top to the slower one, so this is the stamina virtue taken past stock. Paid with absorb 0.68, 35 percent of the span below the floor, which is what polishing the damping ring off actually costs. Loses to slick on absorb and smash.

parts.name: Bolster
parts.desc: A thick fibre pad that swallows a blow whole, and swallows yours as well.
parts.rationale: Sibling of collar. absorb 1.42 is 26 percent of the 0.46 span past 1.30; smash 0.70 is 39 percent of the span below the floor, further, and a soft pad genuinely cannot transmit a hard blow. radAdd matched to collar's 0.0002 and gearMul left worse for a defense build, so it beats collar on absorb and nothing else.

parts.name: Gutta
parts.desc: A soft damping ring that shrugs off impacts and grips everything it meets, so every touch trades spin.
parts.rationale: Sibling of wing. The cleanest physics in the set: damping and friction come from the same material property, so a rim soft enough to reach absorb 1.42 must also be tacky. gearMul 2.35 is 39 percent of the span past 1.80, further than the 26 percent push, and it is a genuine bill for a stamina top because a stamina top is usually the faster one late in a round and mu bleeds the faster rim into the slower one. Note the pay goes up rather than down: gearMul is two sided, and for this build high grip is the liability.

parts.name: Chisel
parts.desc: A heavy blunt wedge that hits like a hammer and drags the heavy side of the top flat.
parts.rationale: Sibling of rake. smash 1.30 is 28 percent of the 0.36 span past 1.20; mass 0.0080 is 38 percent past the 0.0058 ceiling, further. This is the one part where a mass payment is real: imb is |sum| divided by m and R, so 0.0080 kg of extra metal dilutes the imbalance an attack build lives on and flattens imbSwing, imbDrive and imbDash together. Loses to rake on gearMul, radAdd and weight, ties on absorb, wins on smash alone.

parts.name: Eaves
parts.desc: The widest rim in the game, cut from sheet so thin that it folds once the spin is gone.
parts.rationale: Sibling of vane. radAdd 0.0030 is 50 percent of the span past the ceiling, which through load's R exponent of minus 1.24 is roughly a 15 percent decay cut on a Cleaver chassis, the largest single stamina gain the slot can offer. Glass is the right drawback rather than a decoration, because the build this part makes is the one still alive at the end of a long round, so it will spend real time under 40 percent spin with taken doubled. Absorb 0.66 pays on top. Thin sheet is why it is light and why it is glass, which is the same fact told twice.

parts.name: Rasp
parts.desc: Teeth like a coarse file that tear spin off anything they touch and burn through your own.
parts.rationale: Sibling of hook. gearMul 3.00 is 84 percent of the span past 1.80, and hungry multiplies gear by a further 1.40 inside collide, so effective grip reaches about 4.2 against a stock rim. The same drawback raises baseline decay 25 percent every step of the round, so the steal has to outpace the burn or the part loses to itself, which is what keeps the mean honest while the ceiling stays absurd. Absorb 0.70 pays, and mu is a square root of both gears, so the push is naturally sublinear against low grip opponents.

parts.name: Bushing
parts.desc: A soft sleeve that damps every blow and never lets the threads seat tight.
parts.rationale: Sibling of collar. absorb 1.70 is 87 percent of the span past 1.30, cutting tilt per strike by 40 percent against stock and making it the hardest top in the game to knock over. Loose Lock is the same physical fact stated as a cost: the compliant sleeve that swallows the shock is exactly what stops the ratchet teeth seating, so burstResist halves while stable rises 30 percent. Smash 0.72 pays at 33 percent of the span below the floor. Attack answers it with one connected swing, which is the intended matchup.

parts.name: Chert
parts.desc: A knapped stone edge that lands one devastating blow and is blunt for the rest of the round.
parts.rationale: Sibling of rake. smash 1.55 is 97 percent of the span past 1.20; through the jn coefficient of 0.72 plus 0.62 times smash that is about 25 percent more impulse, and wear cubes it, so with One Shot's 3.0 first strike multiplier the opening blow carries roughly six times stock burst wear. Every strike after does 40 percent, so the part is one moment and then nothing, which is exactly the Relic shape. gearMul 0.20 pays at 47 percent below the floor, and it is the honest cost of a knapped face: no teeth means no tangential shove, so it struggles to force the contact it needs.

notes:
SHAPE: each entry needs `tier` and, for Relics, `drawback` added to the ASSISTS array in sim2.js. build() already reads `p.drawback` and `p.tier` generically, so no code change is required for any part here. No new drawback is proposed; all four Relics use drawbacks the simulation already enforces (glass at line 792/795, hungry at 673/774, looselock at 377, oneshot at 819).

HOW I MEASURED "25 PERCENT PAST THE RANGE": as 25 percent of the Tier 1 span beyond the edge. radAdd 0.0025 = +25%, gearMul 2.15 = +24.6%, absorb 1.42 = +26%, smash 1.30 = +27.8%. The one exception is gearMul at the LOW end, where 25 percent of the 1.42 span below 0.38 is a negative number; there I measured proportionally, so lacquer's 0.28 is 26 percent below the floor. Payments sit 33 to 47 percent past the opposite edge in every case, so every pay is deeper than its push.

TWO FACTS FROM THE CODE THAT SHAPED THE NUMBERS, both worth checking before you tune:

1. radAdd is stronger than the brief credits. I = 0.55·m·R² and load = (m/0.035)^0.55 · (iRef/I)^0.62, so load is proportional to m^-0.07 · R^-1.24. radAdd also divides incoming shock (dmg/(def.m·def.R)), divides the tangential spin swing (jt·R/I goes as 1/(mR)), and pushes the weight rings outward since ring radius is a fraction of R. Four systems, one stat. That is why both 0.0025 pushers pay at 35 to 39 percent and the 0.0030 Relic carries Glass on top.

2. Assist mass is close to free for spin. The same exponents give m^-0.07, so filling the slot with metal very slightly LOWERS decay rather than raising it. Mass only bills through imb = |sum| / (m·R), which dilutes the heavy side swing. A mass payment is therefore a real cost on a wobble build and nearly none on a defense grinder. I used mass as the paid stat exactly once, on chisel, an attack part whose damage engine is imbSwing. Everywhere else mass stays inside the Tier 1 range. If you want mass to be a general currency, it needs a term in load with a positive exponent, and that is a sim change, not a catalogue change.

DOMINANCE: every part wins on its pushed stat and only its pushed stat against its Tier 1 sibling. I checked each against all ten stock assists. Where a proposal was drifting toward a free win I trimmed it: longspur's smash went 1.16 to 1.10 and its mass 0.0038 to 0.0042 to stay under jag; sprocket's absorb went 1.08 to 0.98 to stay under hook; bolster's radAdd went to 0.0002 to match collar; bushing's radAdd to 0.0002 for the same reason.

RANKED RISK FOR partaudit.js 800 2, most likely to fail the plus 4 mean gate first:
1. chert. Highest ceiling in the set by a distance. If it fails, trim smash 1.55 to 1.44 before touching anything else; wear is cubic in impulse so a small smash cut moves the burst rate a lot.
2. eaves. The decay cut is large and Glass only fires late. If it fails, absorb 0.66 to 0.62 first, then radAdd 0.0030 to 0.0028.
3. cornice. It is the safest looking part in the set and the one I trust least, because radAdd 0.0025 with mass at the Tier 1 ceiling is two inertia gains at once and smash 0.70 is a cheap bill for a balance build that was never going to finish by ringout. Watch its mean specifically.
4. rasp and bushing should sit low; both drawbacks bill continuously rather than conditionally.

RESERVE LEVER, offered but NOT used by any part above: if eaves clears the gate on ceiling but fails on mean, the cleanest fix is a fifth drawback rather than a stat trim, because the physical objection to a very wide rim is that it catches the lip. Call it `overhang`, "the rim reaches past the dish lip, so it leaves the ring easier", and it is one line inside stepTop's wall block, changing an existing quantity with no special case:
const need = K.exitNeed * g.exitNeed * (s.dw && s.dw.overhang ? 0.70 : 1) * (sector > 0.62 ? K.pocketMu : 1) * (a.t < a.anchor ? 6 : 1);
Applying it would mean eaves carries two drawbacks, so prefer swapping Glass for Overhang rather than stacking them.

COPY: no em dash, en dash or hyphen appears in any name, desc or rationale, and no part code in this slot needs one.
